topic: Are the least skilled really the most overconfident?
subject: psychology

sources.title: Why the Unskilled Are Unaware: Further Explorations of (Absent) Self-Insight Among the Incompetent
Unskilled and unaware--but why? A reply to Krueger and Mueller (2002).
Unskilled and unaware of it: how difficulties in recognizing one's own incompetence lead to inflated self-assessments
Unskilled and Don't Want to Be Aware of It: The Effect of Self-Relevance on the Unskilled and Unaware Phenomenon
The ‘unskilled and unaware’ effect is linear in a real‐world setting

facts.claim: In a study of humor, grammar, and logic, participants in the bottom quartile estimated themselves to be in the 62nd percentile despite scoring in the 12th percentile.
facts.quote: Although their test scores put them in the 12th percentile, they estimated themselves to be in the 62nd.

facts.claim: The unskilled and unaware effect was reduced when the task was perceived to have low self-relevance.
facts.quote: As predicted, the unskilled and unaware effect was attenuated when the task was perceived to have low self-relevance.

facts.claim: In a real-world anatomy exam, students in all quartiles were unable to self-assess their performance, except for a group of mid-range students in the 2nd quartile.
facts.quote: Students in all quartiles were unable to self-assess their exam performance, except for a group of mid-range students in the 2nd quartile.

facts.claim: A meta-analysis showed that poor performers' overly optimistic estimates are linked to a lack of insight into their own errors rather than mistaken assessments of their peers.
facts.quote: An additional meta-analysis showed that it was lack of insight into their own errors (and not mistaken assessments of their peers) that led to overly optimistic estimates among poor performers.

facts.claim: Improving the skills of participants in a study helped them recognize the limitations of their abilities.
facts.quote: Paradoxically, improving the skills of participants, and thus increasing their metacognitive competence, helped them recognize the limitations of their abilities.

rejected.claim: The authors of S2 argue that a regression-BTA account cannot explain the experimental data reported in J. Kruger and D. Dunning or a reanalysis following the procedure suggested by J. Krueger and R. A. Mueller.
rejected.quote: Additionally, a regression-BTA account cannot explain the experimental data reported in J. Kruger and D. Dunning or a reanalysis following the procedure suggested by J. Krueger and R. A. Mueller.

research.angle: While some researchers suggest the pattern is a statistical artifact, multiple studies and meta-analyses indicate it is caused by a lack of metacognitive skill and self-relevance rather than just a regression effect.
research.verdict: The evidence suggests that the unskilled are unaware of their incompetence due to a lack of metacognitive ability, though the effect can be influenced by self-relevance.
research.caveat: The studies vary in setting, ranging from laboratory tests of humor and grammar to real-world high-stakes medical exams.
